Dev / Laura — reviewed. Below is proposed compromise language that I think is commercially reasonable and defensible for Redwood. It (a) provides ProspectCo comfort on serious harms, (b) limits Redwood's open-ended exposure for property damage in a SaaS context, and (c) keeps our existing aggregate cap intact for all other liabilities. Please see the suggested insertion for Section 10 (Limitation of Liability):

  "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitations of liability and exclusions set forth in this Section 10 shall not apply to the extent prohibited by applicable law, nor shall they apply to (i) liability for death or bodily injury caused by a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (ii) liability for physical damage to tangible property directly caused by a party's on-premises equipment or on-site personnel, but only to the extent such damage arises from that party's gross negligence or willful misconduct. For the avoidance of doubt, all other liabilities (including those arising from the provision of hosted SaaS services) remain subject to the monetary caps set forth in this Agreement."

Rationale / notes:
- We do not accept an infinite, uncapped liability for all property damage caused by cloud services — that would be an untenable commercial risk.
- We can accept an uncapped carve-out for death/bodily injury, but we limit it to gross negligence/willful misconduct rather than simple negligence unless statute requires otherwise. That narrows exposure while addressing ProspectCo's core safety concern.
- For on-prem appliances / onsite personnel (the scenario ProspectCo mentioned), the carve-out is limited and conditioned on gross negligence/willful misconduct. That should be acceptable to an enterprise customer while protecting Redwood.
- We should also add a short definition for "on-premises equipment" in the Order Form if they choose the dedicated appliance option.

If you both sign off, I'll prepare a redline (Redwood_MSA_proposed_redline.docx) with the insertion and a short comment explaining our position for Procurement.

Thanks,
